children.value: How Offing's findings compare with Renovate, xeol, and Pluto, and what each disagreement means. The summary and the accuracy table are on

Renovate is the closest widely used tool, so the report compares Offing's findings with Renovate's for the same repository, by rule family. A maintainer runs Renovate (it needs the network and a large download; it is not part of
or any scan). Give it a read-only GitHub token, or it cannot look up GitHub Actions:

export RENOVATE_TOKEN=<token> GITHUB_COM_TOKEN=<token>
npx renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup --report-type=file --report-path=renovate.json
npm run differential:renovate -- --renovate renovate.json --repository . --name owner/repo --out report.json

The two tools answer different questions. Renovate says a newer version exists and prints npm deprecation notices; it has no end-of-life data. Offing says a release line is past its vendor's end of life; it does not say an update exists. So the report only compares where both can speak about one dependency in one file:
Renovate offers an update for the image Offing calls end-of-life
Renovate offers an update for the action Offing flags

) have no Renovate counterpart and are listed as not comparable. Matching is by file and dependency name because Renovate gives no line numbers.
